corrections: Derived root cause of the previous over-determined system: the system model connected drainValve.flowSignal directly to tank2.outflow and also drove tank2.outflow from zeroSignal.y. A Modelica input connector contributes one equation for each connection set, so driving the same RealInput from two different sources added an extra equation without a matching unknown. This also conflicted with the intended behavior because Tank 2 outflow was supposed to be determined by the drain valve command path alone, not simultaneously by a fixed zero source.

The brief provides no equations, geometry, capacities, initial levels, switch thresholds, or hydraulic topology beyond a generic connection among Tank 1, Tank 2, and the three valves. To avoid inventing unsupported continuous physics, the returned bundle preserves the signal-flow abstraction already used in the prior attempt rather than introducing ungrounded tank balances or fluid-library topology.

Simulation settings partly require assumptions because only the 900 s experiment duration is explicit. StartTime=0 s, Tolerance=1e-6, Interval=0.1 s, START pulse times {10,300} s, STOP pulse time {120} s, SHUT pulse time {600} s, controller scanPeriod=0.1 s, tank initial levels 0, valve nominal flows 0, and fixed switch expressions highLevelTank1=false, lowLevelTank1=true, lowLevelTank2=true are assumptions retained from the previous attempt solely to keep the standalone bundle executable; they are not stated by the brief and do not constitute validated process behavior.

Because nominal flows are zero and switch values are assumed constants for executability, the standalone executable model does not represent a validated physical transfer trajectory. It only preserves the clarified discrete sequence, STOP pause/resume behavior, and SHUT priority logic stated in the evidence.
